entry.title: Camera Motion Prompts for AI Image-to-Video: A Practical Cheat Sheet
entry.summary: Most weak image-to-video clips fail for the same reason: the prompt describes the picture again instead of describing the movement. The model can already see your image. What it needs from you is how the camera moves, what moves inside the frame, and what must stay still. This cheat sheet collects the camera moves that work reliably, the wording that tends to produce them, and the mistakes that cause warping and drift. A good image-to-video prompt usually answers three questions, in this order: Camera: How does the camera move? (push in, orbit, pan, static) Subject: What moves in the scene? (hair in the wind, steam rising, a person turning their head) Constraints: What must not change? (the logo, the face, the product shape, the background) Example: Slow push-in toward the cup. Steam rises…

entry.title: What a VAPT report should hand back to your dev team
entry.summary: A penetration test is only useful if developers can act on the result. A long PDF of scanner output does not help anyone ship a fix. Here is what a development team should expect from a vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT), based on how the security team at Affix Center in Mumbai runs these engagements. Infrastructure, applications and APIs, not only the public website Secure configuration reviews of the systems the app runs on Controlled penetration testing, so production is not put at risk A risk-ranked report, so the team knows what to fix first Remediation steps for each finding Both an executive report and a technical report, because managers and developers need different detail A retest after the fixes, to confirm they worked A secure development lifecycle Authentication and authorisation on every API Encryption at rest and in transit Role-based access, with audit and compliance traceability Run VAPT at least once a year, and again after any major change to an application or to infrastructure. If your organisation faces NIC or CERT-In empanelled security audits, plan time to fix the observations those audits raise. That work usually lands on the development team. More detail on scope and process: Cyber Security and VAPT services by Affix Center Written by the team at Affix Center, an IT services company in Lower Parel, Mumbai.
